items.question: According to the GENERAL paragraph of Section 6, within which limits must the helicopter always be flown?
options: Within weight and balance limits specified in Section 2
Within the performance envelopes of Section 5 only
Within the structural load limits of the maintenance manual
Within any limits agreed with the operator
items.explanation: Section 6 GENERAL states that the helicopter must be flown only within the weight and balance limits specified in Section 2.

items.question: What is stated as a possible consequence of loading the helicopter outside the specified weight and balance limits?
options: Excessive fuel consumption
Insufficient control travel for safe operation
Increased cruise speed beyond VNE
Higher main rotor vibration only at high speed
items.explanation: Section 6 warns that loadings outside the specified limits can result in insufficient control travel for safe operation.

items.question: Where may removable ballast be added to adjust center of gravity, according to Section 6?
options: Only in the aft baggage compartment behind the rotor mast
Only in a special ballast box in the tailcone
To any under-seat baggage compartment
Only in the nose compartment ahead of the instrument panel
items.explanation: Section 6 states that the center of gravity may be adjusted by adding removable ballast to any under-seat baggage compartment.

items.question: What must be done after adding removable ballast to adjust the helicopter's center of gravity?
options: No further action is required if ballast is under a seat
Only note the ballast on the flight log if it exceeds 10 lb
Recalculate weight and balance and verify baggage compartment limits are not exceeded
Inform ATC of the new gross weight before takeoff
items.explanation: Section 6 requires that weight and balance be recalculated after adding ballast, and that the ballast be verified against baggage compartment limits given in Section 2.

items.question: Which part of the weight and balance data is explicitly stated as not being subject to FAA approval?
options: The loading instructions only
The detailed weight and balance data of Section 6
The CG limits published in Section 2
The performance charts used for loading calculations
items.explanation: Section 6 explains that, in accordance with FAA procedures, the detailed weight and balance data of this section are not subject to FAA approval, while the loading instructions are approved.

items.question: What caution is given in Section 6 regarding fuel burn and center of gravity?
options: Fuel burn causes CG to move aft, possibly exceeding aft limits
Fuel burn causes CG to move forward, so loading must be checked with both takeoff and empty fuel
Fuel burn does not significantly affect CG and can be neglected
Fuel burn only affects lateral CG and not longitudinal CG
items.explanation: The CAUTION in Section 6 states that fuel burn causes CG to move forward during flight, and that safe loading must be determined with both empty fuel and takeoff fuel; payload may be limited by forward CG as fuel is burned.

items.question: When must a new entry be made in the Weight and Balance Record form according to Section 6?
options: Only when major structural components are changed
Each time an item of equipment is removed or installed
Only when the basic empty weight changes by more than 10 lb
Only after an annual inspection by an authorized mechanic
items.explanation: The WEIGHT AND BALANCE RECORD paragraph specifies that an entry must be made each time an item of equipment is removed or installed, and the new empty CG must be determined.
references: R44 II POH Sec 6: WEIGHT AND BALANCE RECORD (p.6-2)

items.question: What note is given in Section 6 regarding CG with full fuel and a 150 lb pilot?
options: CG with full fuel and 150 lb pilot may be ignored if within gross weight limits
Calculated CG with full fuel and 150 lb pilot must be within CG limits and may require adjustment of fixed nose ballast
It is sufficient to check CG only with empty fuel and pilot weight
CG with full fuel and 150 lb pilot is always within limits and needs no verification
items.explanation: The NOTE in the WEIGHT AND BALANCE RECORD section states that calculated CG with full fuel and 150 lb pilot must be within CG limits and that, following modification, adjustment to fixed nose ballast may be required.
references: R44 II POH Sec 6: WEIGHT AND BALANCE RECORD (p.6-2)

items.question: According to the COMMON ITEM WEIGHT & CG table, which longitudinal arm may be used for combined main and aux fuel when calculating longitudinal CG?
items.explanation: The note under the COMMON ITEM WEIGHT & CG and loading worksheets states that a longitudinal arm of 104.5 in. may be used for combined main and aux fuel when calculating longitudinal CG.
references: R44 II POH Sec 6: LOADING INSTRUCTIONS (p.6-4 to 6-7)

items.question: How is the center of gravity location (arm) for the loaded helicopter determined in the sample loading calculation?
options: By dividing total weight by total moment
By dividing total moment by total weight
By subtracting empty weight from total moment
By averaging the longitudinal and lateral arms
items.explanation: Section 6 explains in the sample loading calculation that CG location (arm) for the loaded helicopter is determined by dividing total moment by total weight.
references: R44 II POH Sec 6: SAMPLE LOADING CALCULATION (p.6-6 to 6-7)
